resources.string: Elamon shows a computer\'s load, temperatures, memory, processes and monitors live. The computer runs a small service that only paired phones can read.
Install the elamond service on the computer (Linux), from the project\'s releases or your distribution.
Start it as a service for your user:
Run this on the computer. It shows a QR code and a six-digit code:
Point this phone\'s camera at the QR code, or tap Add computer here and enter the code.
The easiest way: run elamond pair on the computer and point the phone\'s camera at the QR code it shows.
Or enter the computer\'s address, then the six-digit code.
Check that these digits match the certificate line elamond pair shows on the computer:
Six digits shown by elamond pair
The QR code identified this computer. Pair this phone with it?
The computer doesn\'t answer. Check that the service is running and that the phone is on the same network or VPN.
Something answered at this address, but not with the certificate the computer announced. Pairing was stopped to be safe.
Wrong code. After five wrong codes the computer needs a new one.
The computer isn\'t waiting for a phone. Run elamond pair on it first.
This phone will stop showing it. To see it again, pair again. To also remove the phone on the computer, run elamond revoke there.
The computer may be off or asleep, the service not running, or the phone on another network. Elamon keeps trying.
The computer no longer accepts it, maybe after elamond revoke. Run elamond pair on the computer and pair again.
This happens when the service\'s data was reset or reinstalled, but also when something else pretends to be the computer. If you didn\'t reset it, check your network before pairing again.
Powered down because nothing uses it. Elamon doesn\'t wake it to read it; it shows here when a program starts using it.
Intel graphics don\'t report their load to programs without extra rights; the clock shows how hard it works.
Search by name, command or PID
The computer reports no temperature or fan sensors. Some need a kernel module, often loaded by lm-sensors.
The computer runs without a screen, or its graphics driver doesn\'t report monitors.

Elamon has two parts: this app, and elamond, a small service on the computer you want to watch. The service reads the computer\'s own counters and sends them only to phones you paired with it. It needs no root and runs as a service of your user.

Install git, a C compiler (gcc or clang) and Rust 1.88 or newer, from your distribution or from rustup.rs.
Build the service and install it for your user. Nothing goes outside your home folder:
If the shell doesn\'t find elamond afterwards, ~/.local/bin isn\'t on your PATH; run it as ~/.local/bin/elamond.
The openFirewall option above does it. Without the NixOS module, open the ports yourself:
firewalld is on by default here:
Without a firewall nothing needs opening. If ufw is on:
Without a firewall nothing needs opening. Otherwise open TCP 47823 and UDP 5353 in the one you use.

TCP 47823 is the service itself. UDP 5353 is mDNS, which lets the app find the computer by itself; without it, add the computer by its address. Over a VPN such as Tailscale or WireGuard only 47823 matters, and a trusted VPN interface needs nothing.
It shows a QR code and a six-digit code, good for five minutes. Point the phone\'s camera at the QR code and open the link: that pairs in one tap.

Or in this app tap the computer under Found on this network, or Add computer and its address, and enter the code. The app first shows the computer\'s certificate digits: they must match the Certificate line on the computer.
The computer isn\'t under Found on this network

The phone and the computer have to be on the same network, with UDP 5353 open on the computer. VPNs and many guest Wi-Fi networks block this kind of discovery. Add the computer by address instead: elamond pair shows its addresses.
Check that the service runs, and read its log:
Then check that TCP 47823 is open in the firewall and that the phone can reach the computer\'s address.
It works only while I\'m logged in
A user\'s services stop at logout unless lingering is on:
The app says the certificate changed

The service made a new certificate: its folder ~/.local/share/elamon was deleted, or the system was reinstalled. If so, forget the computer in the app and pair again. If not, something else may be answering at that address; check the network first.
Some sensors need kernel modules. lm-sensors finds and loads them; then restart the service:
The graphics card shows no load

NVIDIA cards need NVIDIA\'s driver, whose management library the service reads. A card marked Sleeping is powered down and is left that way until a program uses it. Intel graphics don\'t report their load without extra privileges, so the app shows the clock instead.
A monitor that is switched off or blanked has no mode. If no monitor shows one, the service can\'t open the graphics device: your user has to be logged in at the computer or be in the video group.
How do I unpair a phone?
In the app: the computer\'s menu, Forget computer. To also drop the phone\'s access on the computer, list the paired phones and revoke one by its ID:
pair a phone: shows a QR code and a code
list paired phones with their IDs
print one reading, to see what the service finds
Optional, in ~/.config/elamon/elamond.toml. Restart the service after a change. The defaults:
the TCP port the app connects to
the address to listen on; \"::\" covers IPv4 and IPv6
the name shown in the app; the host name when empty
announce the service on the local network, so the app finds it
minutes of history a phone gets when it connects
The service keeps its certificate and the paired phones in ~/.local/share/elamon. Deleting that folder unpairs every phone.

The phone talks to your computer directly, encrypted, and trusts only the certificate it saw when pairing. Nothing passes through any server, and the app has no trackers, ads or analytics. Each phone has its own key, which the computer can revoke; keys are kept out of Android backups. The service only reads: it can\'t change anything on the computer.
